sections.markdown:
## C — Distracted driving and electronic communication devices: why driving needs full attention, common distractions, why texting is the riskiest, children, friends and pets, setting controls before driving, roadside gawking, what the device law bans and allows while moving, and how violations are handled
Knowledge domain: what counts as a driving distraction and why it is dangerous, why texting is the most hazardous, how to manage children, friends and pets in the car, how to handle in-vehicle controls and devices safely, why looking at roadside scenes is a distraction, and exactly what Missouri's electronic communication device law prohibits and permits while a vehicle is moving.

FACT_ID: sec17-F01 | anchor: A01
Safe driving needs your full attention, because it involves constant and complex coordination between your mind and your body. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F02 | anchor: A01
A distraction is anything that keeps you from operating the car safely, and every distraction puts drivers, passengers and bystanders at risk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F03 | anchor: A01
The guide's list of distractions includes texting, phone use, eating and drinking, talking to passengers, adjusting audio players, grooming, reading maps, watching videos, browsing the Internet and using navigation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F04 | anchor: A01
Texting takes your eyes, your hands and your mind off driving at once, which makes it by far the riskiest distraction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F05 | anchor: A01
Missouri law forbids anyone to read, write or send a text or other electronic message while operating a vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F06 | anchor: A01
Children, friends and pets can each become a dangerous distraction while you drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F07 | anchor: A01
If your children need attention, pull over to a safe place instead of handling them while driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F08 | anchor: A01
Save arguments and upsetting conversations for a safe place, not for while you are driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F09 | anchor: A01
Secure a pet in a carrier, portable kennel or pet harness while driving, and never let it sit on your lap. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F10 | anchor: A01
Entering a destination, scanning radio stations or changing climate settings can lead to a crash or near-crash, and Internet and email access add more risk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F11 | anchor: A01
Set the climate controls, mirrors, radio and seat before you start to drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F12 | anchor: A01
Check email, voicemail and other devices before you leave or after you arrive, not on the way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F13 | anchor: A01
You can set an auto-reply on your phone saying you are driving and will call back later. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec17-F14 | anchor: A02
Use normal stops to adjust controls, or ask a passenger to adjust the radio, climate or navigation for you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F15 | anchor: A02
Staring at a crash scene, a vehicle stopped by police, a scenic view, a billboard, street addresses or construction work while driving is a distraction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F16 | anchor: A02
Missouri law bars drivers of both commercial and noncommercial vehicles from using an electronic communication device on any highway or property open to public traffic, apart from the allowed uses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F17 | anchor: A02
While the vehicle is moving, you may not hold or support a cellphone with any part of your body. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F18 | anchor: A02
While the vehicle is moving, you may not type, write, send or read text-based messages by hand. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F19 | anchor: A02
While the vehicle is moving, you may not record, post, send or broadcast video, including video calls and social media posts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F20 | anchor: A02
While the vehicle is moving, you may not watch a video or movie. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F21 | anchor: A02
The law lets you make or take voice calls with voice-operated or hands-free features that turn on or off with a single touch or swipe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F22 | anchor: A02
You may talk hands-free through a built-in speaker, in-car Bluetooth, or earbuds or a headset. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F23 | anchor: A02
You may send and receive text-based messages through voice-to-text features. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F24 | anchor: A02
You may use phone GPS navigation, view a map for navigation, and play music, podcasts, broadcasts or digital audio. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F25 | anchor: A02
Before January 1, 2025, a violation of the device law may bring a warning; after that date it may bring an infraction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec17-F26 | anchor: A02
Commercial drivers who violate the device law may be disqualified, and fines and criminal penalties may also apply under state law. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0095]

Misconceptions: hands-free calling is allowed but holding or supporting the phone while moving is not; voice-to-text is allowed but typing or reading texts by hand is not; a video call is banned even though a voice call is allowed; looking at a crash scene is itself a distraction, not harmless curiosity.
Mnemonics: eyes, hands and mind are the three kinds of attention texting steals; set it before you go, not as you drive.
Glossary: distraction means anything that takes attention away from driving safely; electronic communication device means a phone or similar device used to communicate; hands-free means operating a phone without holding it; voice-to-text means dictating a message instead of typing it; infraction means the violation level the guide says may apply once the warning period ended.
Dynamic facts: the device law is described as new in this guide, its warning period ended on a fixed date, and its fines and penalties are set by statute and can change.
